title: Mouse Model of Pressure Ulcers After Spinal Cord Injury
protocol: Sterilize surgical and non-surgical instruments in an autoclave.
Clean the surgical operating table with 70% ethanol.
Warm a heating pad to 37 °C.
Place the heating pad on the operating table.
Cover the heating pad with sterile surgical drapes.
Procure adult (Balb/c) 10-week-old male mice.
Induce anesthesia in each animal using an inhaler beginning with 5% isoflurane.
Decrease to 2-3% isoflurane to maintain sedation for the remainder of the procedures.
Confirm complete anesthesia by eliciting no response to a tail/paw pinch induced nociception stimulation.
Shave the hair over the dorsum (head to tail) with an electric clipper.
Apply depilatory cream to remove remaining hair.
Wash the dorsum with running water/wet scrub.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the corneas to protect the eyes from drying during surgery.
Scrub the skin with three alternative preparations of betadine scrub and 70% ethanol.
Perform a skin incision (~1.0-1.5 cm) along the midline on the back at the level of T8-T12 vertebrae using a scalpel.
Clear the subcutaneous adipose tissue to get access to the paraspinal muscles.
Dissect the paraspinal muscles slowly to expose the spinous processes and laminae on both sides.
Perform a laminectomy by gently peeling off the spinal lamina using microdissecting forceps to expose the spinal cord (T9-T10 vertebrae).
Secure the spinal column at T8 and lift up to exaggerate the spinal curvature.
Section the spinal cord between the T9 and T10 vertebra all the way to the floor of the vertebral canal with fine scissors, ensuring complete transection.
Apply a piece of subcutaneous fat over the laminectomy site.
Suture the paravertebral muscles using continuous suture.
Close the superficial fascia.
Close the skin using suture clips.
Observe bowel movement on the next day post-SCI.
Manage urinary bladder by manual bladder evacuation.
Scrub the back of the animal with betadine and 70% alcohol.

Inject in the dorsal skin near the sacrum a very small volume (10 µL) of 0.125% bupivacaine solution using a 25 G needle at equidistant places ~0.5-1.0 cm apart, in an ellipse around the magnet application site.
Gently lift a skin fold on the back of the mouse and sandwich it between two magnetic discs (5×12 mm diameter, 2.4 g each, 3800 G magnetic force).
Return animals to single cages placed onto a heating pad until full consciousness is regained.
After 12 hours of magnet application, lightly anesthetize the animal with isoflurane.
Remove the magnets from the animal.
Take a photograph of the wound sites to record the initial appearance of PU at day 0.
Cover the wound with transparent dressing film (3M) to avoid drying or contamination.
Immediately after surgery, inject the animal subcutaneously with 1 mL of 0.9% saline for hydration.
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine-SR (1 mg/kg) immediately for analgesia.
Inject subcutaneously meloxicam (1 mg/kg) daily for pain management.
Inject subcutaneously cefazolin (50 mg/kg) for 3-7 days to prevent infection.
Manually evacuate the bladder twice daily.
Provide food and water ad libitum in single cages.
Remove surgical clips 7 days after SCI surgery.
Euthanize animals by CO2 inhalation (3-5 min) at the desired time points after SCI and skin wounding, in accordance with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia.
Collect wounded skin samples.
Fix the samples in 10% formalin for 24 hours.
Store fixed samples in 70% ethanol at 4°C until sectioning.
Embed tissues in paraffin.
Generate thin sections (5 µm) on a microtome.
Stain sections with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).
Perform immunohistochemistry using antibodies for Ki67, CD31, and alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA).
